analysis: Examined the new AdmissionRateEstimators.swift (DeadlineAdmissionFixes kill switch; IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve), the LaunchAgent.swift allowlist addition, and the added test file (metadata only, no body supplied). The change is availability and admission-heuristic scoped: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES is parsed fail-open to enabled, and only explicit 0/false/no/off disable it. It governs first-token deadline admission estimators, not authentication, attestation, encryption, authorization or plaintext handling. No trust-boundary assets (A-001, A-003, A-015, A-016) are touched. LaunchAgent.swift:285 adds the key to inferencePassthroughEnvKeys, which flows into passthroughEnvKeys (lines 292-305) and passthroughEnvironment (lines 319-340). That forwards only a non-empty allowlisted value into the launchd plist's EnvironmentVariables, so a rollback set in the installing shell persists across watchdog and launchd restarts, matching the existing PREFILL_DEADLINE_MODE pattern. No new secrets, paths or arguments are added. In resolve, non-finite or non-positive inputs are sanitized. The anchor floor of 0.125 and the 30-minute stale-evidence expiry bound how far a single contended sample can distort admission. A local operator (ADV-001) who controls the environment could already change admission behavior (the existing PREFILL_DEADLINE_MODE), so this adds no meaningful new capability. Remaining integration questions, not findings: the call sites in EngineV2Bridge and the CBv2 deadline admission code, plus the CBv2DecodeRateShape calibration interaction, were not supplied. Whether the coordinator or consumers could be affected by shifted refusal/admission behavior, such as reduced availability or provider-side admission bias toward serving requests, is unverified. The test file body was not visible, so its coverage is not assessed.
